Transformations.content:
{{header transformations}} '''Transformations''' alter Isaac's appearance and grant him special abilities. A transformation occurs when obtaining at least three different [[item]]s from a particular set of items.
These collectibles always share a particular theme that corresponds with the transformation. == Transformation Sets == {{transformation table}} == Requirements == * Items only need to have been acquired once in order to count. ** {{dlc|nr}} Duplicate items (like those acquired from {{i|Diplopia}}) do not count toward transformations when picked up. Only the first instance of an item Isaac owns will count. ** {{dlc|r}} Duplicate items are all counted. ** {{dlc|r+}} Duplicate items are not counted for the Necromancer transformation. ** [[Activated collectible]]s (e.g. {{i|Guppy's Head}}) can be picked up once and then swapped away with another without any loss to transformation progress. * {{dlc|nr}} Rerolling items with a {{r|Dice Room}}, the {{i|D4}}, or the {{i|D100}} will not remove progress towards the transformation. ** {{dlc|r}} The transformation will be lost if the items required are rerolled or otherwise lost, eg. {{I|Sacrificial Altar|dlc=x}}. * {{dlc+|a}} Familiars gained from {{i|Cambion Conception}} or {{i|Immaculate Conception}} do not count towards transformation progress.{{dlc-}} * [[Trinket]]s do not count toward progress for any transformation, with the exceptions of {{t|Kid's Drawing}} that counts for Guppy transformation, {{t|Bob's Bladder|r+}} for Bob, and {{t|A Missing Page|r+}} for Necromancer. * [[Pill]]s only count toward [[Adult]] and [[Stompy]], they do not count toward progress for any other transformation. * Characters that start with an item that counts towards a transformation do count as one of the three items needed for a transformation, such as Judas starting with [[The Book of Belial]]. * {{dlc+|r}} Only the first character to pick up an item will gain progress towards its transformation. This applies in [[Repentance Co-Op|co-op]], or when playing as {{c|Jacob and Esau}} or {{c|Tainted Lazarus}}.{{dlc-}} * {{C|Tainted Isaac}} will not lose a transformation nor progress towards it if he replaces an item that counts towards that transformation. == Notes == * Transformations can be combined, keeping the effects of all transformations with no effects overriding others. * Transforming into [[Beelzebub]] for the first time will unlock the ''Lord of the Flies'' [[achievement]] and {{i|Angry Fly}}. * {{dlc|a}} As none of the Afterbirth transformations unlock an achievement or item, obtaining them is not required for 100% completion of the game in terms of achievements. However, this is only true if you unlocked {{i|Mom's Contacts}} on Rebirth, as the [[Yes Mother?]] transformation will happen once you collect three Mom items on Afterbirth and Afterbirth †. * {{dlc|nr}} Many of the Afterbirth transformations override the charge animations of items such as {{i|Monstro's Lung}} and {{i|Brimstone}}, potentially making them more difficult to use. ** {{dlc|a+}} There is now an option to show a charge bar that floats above Isaac. == Gallery == File:Transformations Afterbirth.jpg|Concept art drawn for transformations that would be implemented into the Afterbirth DLC. == Trivia == * In the original ''The Binding of Isaac'' flash game, the transformation into [[Guppy]] was the only one available, making it chronologically the first. ** Rebirth introduced [[Beelzebub]] as the chronologically second transformation. ** Made after Rebirth, the ''Eternal Edition'' of the original ''The Binding of Isaac'' game added another transformation that turned Isaac into an angel after gaining 7 heart containers from [[eternal heart]]s. * The original name for the [[Beelzebub]] transformation was Lord of the Flies. * The reason no new transformations were added to Repentance is because at the time Edmund and the dev team did not like them, as they viewed them as significant advantages gained only from being lucky enough to find specific items. This is why Guppy, the most powerful transformation, requires much more effort to get compared to a transformation like Spider Baby. If any new transformations were to be added for Repentance, they would be purely visual.https://youtu.be/N-tWNv5EJkU?t=2623 == References == {{Reflist}} {{nav}} [[Category:Transformations| ]]

The '''Donation Machine''' is a type of machine that appears in almost every {{R|Shop}} as well as rarely spawning through {{R|Black Market}}s, {{g|Reward Plate}}s, {{R|Arcade}}s, and {{R|Vault}}s.

Touching the Donation Machine donates a coin from Isaac's inventory, increasing the displayed coin total by one. Similar to the {{e|Greed Donation Machine}}, the number of coins donated persists between runs. Donating enough money [[Donation Machine#Donation Rewards|upgrades the Shop, the Library, and unlocks new items]].

It takes many runs of continuous donations to unlock everything, as the player will have to donate a total of 999 coins to max the machine out.

== Mechanics ==
A total of 999 coins can be donated. Attempting to donate a 1,000th coin causes the Donation Machine to explode, resetting its total back to 0 and dropping roughly 12 dimes.

Donating money has a chance to jam the machine, preventing further donations. If a machine jams, all future Donation Machines will be jammed as well for the remainder of the run. On average, Donation Machines accept 30 coins before jamming.
* {{dlc|nr}}Each coin has a 5% chance to jam the machine.
* {{dlc|r}} The first coin has a 0.15% chance to jam the machine, increasing by 0.15% with each coin donated on the current floor. Restarting a run with {{i|R Key|n}} un-jams all Donation Machines.

Exploding the Donation Machine, such as with a {{E|Bomb}}, causes it to drop {{dlc|nr}} 1-5 pennies / {{dlc|r}} 6-14 pennies. This decreases the donation total by (number of dropped pennies + 1), resulting in a net loss.
* {{dlc|nr}} The Donation Machine can be exploded for as long as there are still coins inside. It drops coins even when jammed.
** {{i|Humbleing Bundle|nr}} turns the dropped pennies into double pennies, which makes a profit.
* {{dlc|r}} Bombing a Donation Machine destroys it, preventing future Donation Machines from appearing for the rest of the run. The dropped coins are deducted from the donation total at the start of the next run.
** Jammed donation machines cannot be blown up and will not drop any coins.
** Using {{i|R Key|n}} un-explodes the Donation Machine, allowing it to spawn again.

Under rare conditions, it's possible to spawn multiple donation machines in the same room, via {{g|Reward Plate}}s or {{i|TMTRAINER}}. Adding coins to one does not update the coin counter on the others, until the current room is left and re-entered. They can be individually jammed/exploded without affecting the others.

=== Other Effects ===
* Donations have a 2% chance to increase Isaac's luck by 1.
** Donating ten coins to a Donation Machine increases the odds of an {{R|Angel Room}} appearing instead of a {{R|Devil Room}}, if a devil deal was not previously taken. This does not increase the chance overall, instead simply swaying the odds in favor of an Angel Room.
* Donation Machines cannot appear while achievements are disabled.
* {{dlc|r}} Donated money also reduces the chance for {{E|Greed}} to spawn for the next floor: -1.66% per coin, up to a maximum of -8.33% for 5 coins
* {{dlc|r}} Destroying the the Donation Machine increases the chance for {{E|Greed}} to spawn for the next floor by +3.33%

== Donation Rewards ==
{{achievement text | Blue Map, Store Upgrade lv.1, There's Options }}
** Also unlocks {{i|More Options}}.

== Strategy ==
After reaching 999 coins and unlocking everything, the Donation Machine can be exploded freely, essentially letting Isaac trade bombs for the stowed away coins.
* Causing the Donation Machine to explode by reaching 1000 cents is not recommended, as it does not unlock anything and limits the ability to trade bombs for coins in future runs until the coin total has been built back up again.
* It is recommended to deliberately bomb the Donation Machine such that the banked total is less than 999 cents. This effectively prevents accidental 1000th cent donations.

{{dlc|nr}} With items that let Isaac reliably create explosions, such as {{I|Ipecac}}, and {{I|Dr. Fetus}}, the donation machine can be endlessly bombed for as long as there are still coins inside of it, as it doesn't get destroyed after a single explosion like it does in Repentance runs. This can have game-breaking potential, especially if combined with items like {{i|Humbleing Bundle}}, {{i|D20}}, {{P|Jera}}, and {{i|Restock}}.

=== Making Money ===
Though it is generally best to donate coins in addition to playing the game normally (to obtain other unlocks/[[Completion Marks|completion marks]] in addition to filling it up), if the player wishes to deliberately farm coins to fill the Donation Machine sooner, there are multiple ways to do so.
* {{e|Blood Donation Machine}}s/{{i|IV Bag}} can generate a lot of money, at the cost of health.
** If there's an abundance of {{E|Red Heart}}s on the floor (or {{i|Placenta}} and a lot of patience), enough money can be generated with blood donations to jam the machine.
* {{C|Azazel}}'s powerful attack and innate flight makes it easy for him to clear rooms and fly to otherwise hard to reach coins, making him a good choice for farming coins early on.
** {{C|Keeper}} and {{C|Tainted Keeper}} can get a lot of money incredibly fast with their unique starting items and abilities, though by the time they (and Keeper's starting items) are unlocked, it is likely that a high donation total would already be achieved. Regardless, they're still great at refilling the machine for the benefit of future runs.
* {{dlc|ana+}} In versions of the game prior to [[Booster_Packs#Booster_Pack#5|Booster Pack #5]], {{i|Glowing Hourglass}} un-jams the machine and returns the donated coins, but the donation total still goes up as if they were donated. There are multiple ways to donate indefinitely with this, usually by charging it up before leaving the room:
** Purchasing (or otherwise acquiring) a {{E|Lil' Battery}} to recharge Glowing Hourglass in the shop will rewind to back before the battery was purchased.
** Using {{i|Sharp Plug}} (or {{i|Habit}} and two bombs) with more than two hearts provides a full charge.
** If Glowing Hourglass is for sale in the Shop, it can be bought before donating, then used to go back before it was purchased.
** Using a {{p|? Card}}, which takes Isaac back to before it was used, allowing infinite uses of Glowing Hourglass.

* {{dlc|na+}} '''Force Quit Method''': This is an easy way to fill up the machine potentially in one run. This method also has no item prerequisite. The game saves the normal and Greed Donation Machine data separately from your main save file; the machine data is only changed and saved AFTER you leave the room.
** Enter a room with the Donation Machine. Then exit to the start menu normally to save your game.
** Continue the game.
** Donate money until machine jams or you run out of coins.
** Walk out to a different room. Now the game will save the change in coins only.
*** On computer, you will not need to leave the room but will need to suspend the game using an application such as Process Explorer (for Windows)
** Force quit the game
*** Windows: Alt+F4
*** OS X: Force Quit
*** Linux: Ctrl+Alt+Esc (may depend on desktop environment)
*** Consoles: home button and then quit app
** Restart and continue the game. Your save game from the 1st step will be restored. It should look the same as before: the Donation Machine is unjammed, but the starting coin count on the Donation Machine is now higher.
** Donate money. Walk to different room. Force Quit. Repeat.
** Notes: If you accidentally walk by the machine at 999 coins and blow it up by accident, do not leave the room and just Force Quit. The machine will be back at 999.
*** Despite the 5% jam chance noted above, in actuality, the number of coins it takes to jam a machine is set per floor. Let's say it takes 10 coins to jam the machine. If you Force Quit and try again, it will still take 10 coins to jam the machine even with the higher coin count. When you go to the next floor, let's say it now takes 20 coins to jam the machine. Force quitting on the next floor will still take 20 coins to jam the machine next time. The method works best on a Donation Machine that accepts a large number of coins before jamming.

Internally, pills are given a class from 0 to 3 and a polarity that reflects their influence: Pills in class 0 have little to no impact on a run overall, while pills in higher classes are correspondingly more influential, class 3 pills having effects as significant as permanent stat changes. Classes that end with + or - denote a positive or negative effect, otherwise considered neutral. Polarity is used by certain items to determine which pills to convert. Five class 3, two class 2, two class 1, and one class 0 pill effects are guaranteed to be chosen in each run. The remaining three pill effects have random classes. Consequently, the average run is expected to draw, in total: * ~5.84 positive pills * ~4.15 negative pills * ~3.01 neutral pills Polarity is not considered when drawing pill effects; it is therefore possible that only bad pill effects are chosen over this entire process, at an astronomically low chance of 1 in 5,799,273,480. With average luck, slightly less than one third of your pills should be bad ones. During a {{mode|greed}}Greed Mode run, the Amnesia, ???, and Telepills effects cannot be chosen; otherwise, it uses the same system as above. {{dlc-}} == {{dlc+|r}} Gold Pills == [[Repentance]] introduces '''Gold Pills''' (or Golden Pills). Using one gives a random pill effect. Gold pills are unique in that they can be used multiple times, with each use only having a 10% chance to remove the pill. This often allows many uses before they finally disappear. * Unlocked by: {{achievement unlock|Gold Pill}}. * The possible effects are all effects that aren't in the run's pill pool, which means if you see an effect from a normal pill, you will never see it from a gold pill. * Items such as {{I|PHD}} or {{I|Lucky Foot}} which alter pill effects also work on the effects of this pill, allowing many beneficial effects to be stacked with little risk. Effects altered by these items may overlap with the effects in the run's pill pool; for example, a run might have Tears Up in the pill pool and Tears Down outside of the pill pool, which will be turned into Tears Up due to the effects of the item. * Gold Pills have an ID of 5.70.14. * A Gold Pill can also be a Horse Pill. Gold Horse Pills use the Horse Pill effect on every use. * Gold horse pills are most likely the rarest pickup in the game with a 0.06% chance of spawning instead of a normal pill. * If a Gold Pill uses the 'Vurp' effect, and no other pill was used prior, another gold pill will drop. {{dlc-}} == {{dlc+|r}} Horse Pills == ''[[Repentance]]'' introduces '''Horse Pills'''. These are larger versions of the standard pills with a more powerful effect, but only appear very rarely. Unique sound effects can be heard when they are used, and the narrator's normal spoken voice lines are instead shouted using a different voice. * Unlocked by: {{achievement unlock|Horse Pill}}. * All items that work with pills work identically with horse pills. * A horse pill with a given effect has the same color as the normal pill does. * Horse pills have an ID of the normal ID + 2048 (i.e. 1 << 11). For example, a white-blue pill has an ID of 2, so the horse pill version would have an ID of 5.70.2050. * It is also possible to have a golden horse pill. (It has an ID of 5.70.2062.) {{dlc-}} == Probabilities == Pills that spawn with a sub-type of 0 (i.e. a random pill) will have the following probabilities: * Random normal pill - 97.86% * Specific normal pill - 7.53% * Gold pill - 0.7% * Random horse pill - 1.43% * Specific horse pill - 0.11% * Gold horse pill - 0.01% == Notes == * Among the [[attribute]]-modifying pill effects, only five of the seven [[attribute|visible attributes]] are covered: health, range, tears, speed, and luck. The '''Greed Donation Machine''' appears after every [[Ultra Greed]] fight in [[Greed mode]] or {{dlc|a+}} [[Greedier mode]]. Upon touching the Greed Donation Machine, Isaac will donate a coin, causing the displayed coin total to increment. Similar to the [[Donation Machine]], the amount of coins donated will persist between all Greed mode runs. Donating money to the Greed Donation Machine unlocks achievements and items.

== Jam Chance ==
* The machine can be jammed, like the [[Donation Machine]], when adding [[coin]]s. However, rather than a flat 5% chance, the chance increases the more money is put into the machine with a specific [[character]].
* Each character's overall donation status is tracked separately across all playthroughs, so each character has a separate jam chance.
** Characters introduced by mods have a 99.9% (displayed as 100%) chance to jam the machine
** The jam chance maxes out at 20% at 200 coins total in Greed mode, and 1% at 55 coins total in Greedier mode.
** The jam chance updates in real time, so even with a character that has never donated to the donation machine prior, the machine will most likely eventually jam given enough donations.
** The amount of coins added will persist across both Greed and Greedier runs.
** In multiplayer, the HUD will display the jam chance of Player 1's character, but the machine itself uses the jam chance of the character that touches it.
* Like the [[Donation Machine]], if a 1,000th coin is donated, the Greed Donation Machine will explode, dropping several dimes. However, unlike the Donation Machine, donating the 1,000th coin is required to fully complete the game.
* The formula used to convert the total coins donated by the current character to a jam percentage is <math display="inline">floor(0.2*min(100.0, exp(0.023*Coins)-1)+0.5)</math>.
* If the Greed Donation machine is spawned outside of the [[Ultra Greed]] Arena then the machine cannot jam.
** Greedier Mode further caps the percentage to 1% after the calculations.

== Greed Donation Machine Rewards ==
{{achievement text | Lucky Pennies, Special Hanging Shopkeepers, Wooden Nickel, Cain holds Paperclip, Everything is Terrible 2!!!, Special Shopkeepers, Eve now holds Razor Blade, Greedier!, Store Key, Lost holds Holy Mantle, Generosity, Keeper }}

== Greed Donation Machine Tricks ==
* Here are a few ways to drastically shorten the time spent on Greed mode by allowing the player to donate as many coins as possible in a single run.

=== Infinite Money ===
==== Via the 2 of Diamonds ====
# Acquire a {{p|2 of Diamonds}} card and  {{i|Blank Card}} (which must be unlocked first).
# Find a [[Lil' Battery]] for sale. At least 6 or {{dlc|r}} 11 coins are needed to exploit the {{p|2 of Diamonds}} card (11 or {{dlc|r}} 21 coins are needed if the{{i|Blank Card}} is completely uncharged).
# Use the Blank Card to double your money then buy the Lil' Battery to recharge the Blank Card. {{Dlc|r}}You need to buy 2 lil' Batteries because of recharge time 12 rooms instead of 4 rooms (see the {{i|Blank Card}} page); {{t|Butter!}} makes Blank Card revert back to a 4 room charge, making the process as how it was before Repentance. Restock will cause the Lil' Battery to constantly be restocking in the Shop. This allows Isaac to generate an infinite amount of money.
# {{dlc|nr}} Jera can likewise be exploited in the same manner with coins on the ground and can duplicate Lil' Batteries in the shop for ease of exploitation. See {{i|Clear Rune}} (must be unlocked)

This method can be used to quickly gain the Chaos Card as well:
* Use a {{i|Deck of Cards}} and buy Lil' Batteries until you draw a Chaos Card.
** '''Make sure your coin count does not drop below 11 while doing this!'''

==== Via Head of the Keeper ====
* Acquire the {{i|Head of the Keeper}} and keep some enemy spawning monster(s) (like [[Ulcer]]) alive.
* Keep killing spawned monsters until the total amount of desired coins has been spawned from your coin tears.
** However Head of the Keeper will make the fight against Ultra Greed more difficult by constantly producing coins next to him, allowing him to recover some HP regularly.
* Also, your tears will blend in with all the coins Ultra Greed produced, making it difficult to know who is shooting whom. {{dlc|r}}The Bullet Visibility option can assist with the blending in of the tears.

==== Via the D20 ====
* Buy the D20.
* Kill an entire floor without picking up money.
* Restock the Shop until a [[Lil' Battery]] is present.
* Reroll the money. (DON'T TOUCH ANYTHING YET!)
* Buy the [[Lil' Battery]].
* Open all the chests.
* If you don't already have at least 5 cents, pick up coins until you have at least 5 cents.
* Reroll and repeat the process.
* This method is less viable in Repentance, since empty chests no longer can be rerolled.
* This method is more difficult to start in Repentance+, since D20 is now very rare in the {{ip|Greed Shop|text=Greed Shop pool}}.

After a couple of rerolls, you will have 99 of all consumables. This is improved by also having {{i|Mom's Key}}, as you will also get a lot of items from [[Locked Chest]]s.

==== Via Swallowed Penny or Piggy Bank ====
* Acquire the {{t|Swallowed Penny}} or {{i|Piggy Bank}}.
* Acquire any method to regenerate health: {{i|Pyromaniac}} with sufficient/infinite bombs (with sufficient bombs, there's high probability you'll manage to find any number of combos to continue anyway), {{t|Bloody Penny}}, {{i|Scapular}}, Habit with any number of consumable-spawning items, etc.
* Alternatively, acquire {{i|Humbleing Bundle}}, which makes you drop more coins than it costs to heal, [[Steam Sale]], which lowers the margin on healing, or {{i|Maggy's Bow}}, which would heal you for more.
* Take damage, collect coins and health, repeat as required.
* Be careful not to get damage-prevention effects when doing this: Holy Mantle prevents the curse room from damaging you for this purpose, Yes Mother? transformation tend to destroy fires if you aren't careful, {{i|Pyromaniac}} prevents you from using bombs for self-damage, flying prevents you from taking damage from spikes, etc.
* BUT, keep in mind you can always stand in the doorway of a curse room to take damage without exiting the current room (if you have flight this will only work when you stand in the door way from inside the curse room). {{dlc+|r}} The spikes can be removed with {{T|Flat File}}, so be cautious.{{dlc-}}

==== Via IV Bag ====
* Manage to start the game with Eden holding {{i|IV Bag}}.
* Have at least 2 Red Heart containers.
* Keep using the [[IV Bag]] and filling Red Hearts from the Shop. The price of Red Hearts is 3 cents and usually, the [[IV Bag]] gives you 1 or 2 cents per half a heart. Though part of this depends on luck (literally), in the long run, you will be able to get a margin since the [[IV Bag]] gives you Nickels or Dimes time by time.
* Use the margin to purchase collectible items or trinkets.
* {{i|PHD}}, {{t|Swallowed Penny}}, {{t|Counterfeit Penny}}, {{t|Bloody Penny}} will guarantee success on this method and cut down the effort considerably.
* {{i|Placenta}} can be used as an emergency option.
* If there is the [[Lil' Battery]] in the Shop you will be able to produce all the trinkets once you encounter {{i|Mom's Box}}.

=== Notes on Farming Methods ===
* Avoid the following items whenever possible:
** DO <u>NOT</u> get {{i|Missing No.}}. It will cause you to reroll your items and ruin the entire strategy.
** DO <u>NOT</u> get the {{i|Little Baggy}} at all, as it will replace your Two of Diamonds and/or chaos cards.
** {{i|Chaos}}: Will make it a lot harder (nearly impossible) to find {{i|Glowing Hourglass}}, it's best to find it before picking up Chaos.
** {{i|Marked}}: Will force you to shoot tears, which with too many items may result in the game repeatedly crashing, not allowing you to continue. {{dlc|r}}Shooting can be toggled on and off.
* Resetting the Ultra Greed fight many times may cause a bug that strips you of all your items. When this happens, ''close the program via Task Manager. DO NOT use the Hourglass or exit the game normally.'' If you do, the game will save your progress and you will be permanently stripped of your items.
* Be extremely careful when the giant chest spawns since touching it (either by walking into it or being knocked into it by an explosive blast) will immediately end your run.
* Spread your runs out across multiple characters.
** Since the Greed Donation Machine's chance of jamming is character-specific it's a good idea to play multiple characters to decrease the chance of the Greed Donation Machine jamming. If you're having a hard time with the above methods or just don't want to do them, switch characters when you notice the Greed Donation Machine starts jamming regularly on you.

=== Glowing Hourglass Method ===
{{dlc|na+}} '''Methods based on {{i|Glowing Hourglass}} work only in Afterbirth and have been patched in later DLCs.'''

This method centers around the fact that the Greed Donation Machine is unjammed every time Ultra Greed is killed but the coin count doesn't reset after the {{i|Glowing Hourglass}} is used.
In order to make this possible, you will need some way to recharge your spacebar item, since you will only get one recharge every time you kill Ultra Greed. This is also a very good method to farm as many [[Eden]] tokens as you want, as one token will be granted for each Ultra Greed kill.

# Buy the Glowing Hourglass.
#* The Glowing Hourglass is very rare, but it can be found easier by exhausting the shop pool with any of the Infinite Money methods found above.
#* Since {{i|Chaos}} causes each newly generated item to be chosen from a randomly selected item pool, acquiring it should be avoided. Glowing Hourglass is in only one item pool in Greed Mode.
# The fight with Ultra Greed '''has to be started with a fully charged Glowing Hourglass'''.
From here is where you can start donating infinitely:
# Kill Ultra Greed. If the battle looks like a loss, the Glowing Hourglass can be used once to reset the fight, but the next time Ultra Greed has to be defeated in order to keep the combo up.
#* A double-charged Hourglass with {{i|The Battery}} allows infinite uses of the Hourglass, allowing you to reset as much as you want any time.
# Donate money to the Greed Donation Machine until the machine jams.
# Use the Glowing Hourglass to reset back to the room before Ultra Greed.

==== Acquiring the [[Chaos Card]] ====
The Chaos Card (if unlocked already) will allow the player to instantly kill Ultra Greed, cutting a large amount of time otherwise needed to defeat him.
* Keep buying cards from the shop until a Chaos Card shows up.
* Use a {{i|Deck of Cards}} and buy Batteries until you draw a Chaos Card.
** Any [[Lil' Battery|Lil' Batteries]] and Battery Items will further increase the effectiveness of the Deck of Cards.

==== Faster alternative method using the [[0 - The Fool]] card ====
* Acquire an infinite {{i|Glowing Hourglass}} (such as by using {{i|The Battery}}, {{i|Habit}} with any form of self-damage, Glitter Bombs, or the 48 Hour Energy pill), but bring 0 - The Fool card instead of the Chaos Card.
* Kill Ultra Greed once, then run near the bottom of the room to spawn the machine by where the door was, but do NOT donate to the machine.
* Use 0 - The Fool card, re-enter the Boss Room, Ultra Greed will be dead but the machine will still be there, donate to the machine until it breaks.
* Use The Glowing Hourglass, re-enter the room, donate again. Repeat.

=== Force Quit Method ===
{{plat|Switch}} '''This method only applies to the cartridge Switch version, others have been patched.'''

The Force Quit method is an easy way to fill up the Greed Donation Machine. It follows the same exploit as the [[Donation Machine]]. The game saves the Greed and Donation Machine data separately from your main save file; the Machine data is only changed and saved AFTER you leave the room. Requisite is any item or card that allows you to teleport outside the Boss Room. There is no need for Glowing Hourglass, Blank Card, or ? Card for this method as you can reset your items and keep the coin count going higher.
* Defeat Ultra Greed(ier).
* After the Greed Donation Machine appears, exit to the start menu normally to save your game.
* Continue the game.
* Donate money until machine jams or you run out of coins.
* Teleport outside the room. Now the game will save the change in coins only.
* Force quit the game
** Nintendo Switch: eject and reinsert the cartridge
* Restart and continue the game. Your save game from the 2nd step will be restored. It should look the same as before: Greed Donation Machine is unjammed and your teleport item/card is still there, except the starting coin count on the Greed Donation Machine is now higher.
* Donate money. Teleport. Force Quit. Repeat.
* Note: The Force Quit Method has been patched except for the cartridge on Nintendo Switch. The Greed Donation Machine will no longer be there when you return to the game after force quitting, neither will the item/card, which you used to teleport with.
